The stock pulled back 4.92% in its most recent session after tagging a 52-week high three sessions earlier -- I could not confirm a specific negative catalyst for that single-session drop through today's degraded news feed, so I am treating it as digestion after a strong run (RSI 61.5, not overbought; still above both the 50- and 200-day averages) rather than a broken thesis, and sizing/stopping so that I am proven wrong cheaply if it is more than that.
